The author specifies a 500 mm boom. The element positions span 470 mm from reflector to director. Published gain is 4.72 dBd and front-to-back ratio is 16.5 dB. The series guide gives a typical feed gap of 10–12 mm and states the element lengths tip to tip. The short build uses removable halves. Their blanks depend on the connectors.
Broadband 50 Ω version for 430–440 MHz. The author lists 8.7 dBd gain and specifies a choke with three turns of RG-178 on Ø20 mm PVC.

For a 50 Ω feed, the author uses two 75 Ω quarter-wave sections in parallel. Published length per section is 120 mm for RG-179 (VF 0.70), 115 mm for solid PE, and 141 mm for foam PE (VF 0.82). Published gain at 432.000 MHz is 9.1 dBd.

Type 1 uses one feed point for both bands. The 70 cm open-sleeve element is 22 mm from the driven element. The author gives 4.1 dBd at 145.000 MHz and 5.4 dBd at 435.000 MHz for the 2+2 design. Those values describe the published design. Import your measurements separately for 144–146 and 430–440 MHz.
Mounting with standard insulators. The table includes the mounting correction. Check the feed by measuring SWR.
Schematic top view. Each bend is 100 mm from the feed centre. The tips point towards the reflector and are approximately 188 mm from it along the boom. The drawing shows the feed gap schematically.
The source leaves some blank lengths unspecified. See the notes in this record.
Connect two identical 75 Ω quarter-wave sections in parallel between the feed line and the antenna. Choose one of the cable options below.

Measure the distance between the metal ends with the tubes seated against their stops. For a custom spacer, you can choose a 10 mm gap following the DK7ZB lightweight series. The length of each half is (span − gap) / 2.

Enter the gap between the metal ends, the distance from feed centre to the bend and the tip setback towards the reflector along the boom. Cut lengths are calculated separately for H and V. Check the assembled antenna by measuring SWR.
Driven-element cut lengths are based on the entered dimensions. Check them against your feed assembly before cutting.
Enter a valid dimension. The gap can be up to 100 mm and must leave room before the bend. The bend must be within the half-span and the setback within the distance to the reflector.

The boom uses ½″ Schedule 40 PVC pipe. Hose clamps secure the 25.4 mm tape to the cross fittings. Check the center-to-center spacing after seating the pipes in the fittings.
A U-shaped copper hairpin of AWG 12 or 14 wire connects across the driven-element terminals. The wire blank is 127 mm long and the outside width is 19.05 mm. Six turns of RG-58 are wound on the boom.
Dimensions are from sheets 2 and 3 of the NT1K drawing. The 15.875 mm gap is derived from the full span and the two half lengths. Adjust the gap by sliding the halves in their mounts.
Simulation requires a model of the tape and hairpin feed. The segmentation calculator supports straight round elements.
NT1K reported an SWR of 1.12 at 147.054 MHz for a build with a gap of about 25.4 mm. The analyzer was connected at the end of the feedline. Measure SWR after assembling your antenna.
Tape lengths and center positions come from the drawing. Offsets set the overall boom length. Check the assembly drawing for the lengths of pipe between fittings.
The driven length is specified per half. The cut allowance applies to the reflector and director blanks.
